verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean defines the radial patch by transporting the endpoints rather than by taking the set image: radialWindow F XR .mean = Ioo (√(2·left)) (√(2·right)), where window F XR .mean = Ioo (left) (right) is the Lean's I_mean (the `.mean` slot of the four reserved slots; its offsets -8/-3 sit strictly to the right of the `.positive` slot's -14/-9, matching the paper's sup I_pos < inf I_mean). The rewriting: X ↦ √(2X) is strictly increasing and continuous on [0,∞), so the image of an interval Ioo a b with 0 ≤ a is exactly Ioo √(2a) √(2b); hence the Lean set equals the paper's {√(2X) : X ∈ I_mean} whenever the window is nonnegative. The Lean also fixes I_mean as an open interval (the paper does not display its endpoint convention here), and ReservedPatches.radial_mem_window records the inverse direction R ∈ radialWindow ⇒ R²/2 ∈ window, i.e. the paper's X = R²/2.
